title: CYBRIK Suite W1 soc.get_alert_context R0 accepted contract packet manifest
description: Inventory, provenance and compatibility record for the smallest W1 capability-specific contract for soc.get_alert_context. It is additive to existing accepted packets and changes none of their bytes. This contract defines business payload shape only: no endpoint, transport binding, capability registry entry, Fabric invocation grant, runtime implementation, stable bundle tag or release certification. Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION on 2026-07-26; implementation has not started, CI is not wired, and no runtime behavior is proven.
wire_scope: BUSINESS PAYLOAD ONLY. No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, MCP, endpoint, queue, transport or service discovery surface is proposed by this packet.

authority_boundaries.fabric: Fabric tool-grant authority remains exclusively in the separately accepted capability/delegation/policy/approval/execution-receipt chain. A capability name/version/digest pin identifies requested behavior but is not an invocation grant. This business payload contains no execution grant, approval, delegation chain, token, credential or receipt.
authority_boundaries.w2f: W2-F inference delegation is the internal SOC-to-Cyber-AI inference trust seam. It cannot authorize a Fabric tool invocation, cannot widen SOC tenant/org/clearance scope, and cannot be presented as a tool grant for soc.get_alert_context.
authority_boundaries.soc: SOC derives authoritative tenant, org scope, actor, clearance and alert visibility from authenticated policy. Body fields are advisory copies that must match authoritative values; a mismatch fails closed.
authority_boundaries.ai: Cyber AI may consume an authorized, digest-bound result as untrusted analysis context. The result grants no planning, response, approval or execution authority.

data_and_privacy_boundary.digest_binding: Request and available result both bind the SOC alert by sha256 digest; runtime must reject a mismatch, stale substitution or cross-object replay.
data_and_privacy_boundary.clearance: Result data_marking must not exceed request clearance on either classification or TLP axis. Runtime enforcement is mandatory and is not proven by schema validation.
data_and_privacy_boundary.no_existence_leak: Unavailable covers absent, unauthorized and policy-filtered resources with the single alert_context_unavailable code and no resource reference, context, reason or existence bit.
data_and_privacy_boundary.org_scope: Result tenant/org scope and authorized actor must match the authoritative request scope, including include_descendants and full actor type/id/tenant/delegated_by identity. include_descendants is a request, never self-authorizing.
data_and_privacy_boundary.safe_internal_refs: Alert/event/entity/case references are closed type/id/version/digest objects with additionalProperties=false and no locator field. Resolution occurs only inside the authenticated SOC boundary; caller-supplied URL/locator fetching is forbidden.

canonicalization.standard: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS), UTF-8 bytes, SHA-256, lowercase hex rendered as sha256:<64-hex>.
canonicalization.owner: The authenticated SOC capability implementation produces request input, authorization binding and available-result context digests after credential authorization and field-level redaction. Fabric may verify/receipt them but does not redefine the projections.
authorization_binding_projection: schema_digest = SHA-256 of exact capability schema bytes

idempotency_semantics.order: Validate credential -> derive authoritative tenant/org/full actor/clearance -> authorize capability and alert scope -> compute schema/input/policy/binding digests -> only then perform a tenant-partitioned idempotency/cache lookup. Authorization-before-cache is mandatory.
idempotency_semantics.cache_partition: Partition by authoritative tenant plus idempotency_key; a cache hit is usable only when the stored authorization_binding.binding_digest equals the freshly computed binding digest.
idempotency_semantics.replay: Same tenant + same idempotency_key + exact same binding digest returns the exact stored result bytes and marks idempotency_disposition=replayed. Authorization is still recomputed before lookup.
idempotency_semantics.conflict: Same tenant + same idempotency_key + different binding digest rejects before target lookup as outcome=idempotency_conflict, idempotency_disposition=conflict, code=idempotency_binding_conflict, retryable=false; it returns no alert_ref/context/context_digest and reveals no cached or target-derived state.
idempotency_semantics.unavailable_derivation: Unavailable response fields derive only from the request plus credential-derived authorization/policy metadata. They never derive from target existence, denial reason, stored context or cache contents; timing/observable equivalence remains a runtime-only obligation.

structural: TI-1 Capability identity is pinned to soc.get_alert_context, R0 and side_effects=false.
TI-2 Request/result tenant, org, actor, clearance/data-marking and digest-bearing fields are explicit and additionalProperties=false.
TI-3 Fabric execution-grant fields and W2-F delegation-token fields are rejected from the business payload.
TI-4 Unavailable results expose exactly one generic caller-visible code and prohibit alert_ref, context and context_digest.
TI-5 Every alert/event/entity/case reference is a digest-bound objectRef; no arbitrary public URL or inline raw telemetry field is introduced.
runtime_only_fixture_exercised: TR-1 Credential-derived actor tenant must equal request tenant; the structurally valid cross-tenant actor fixture must be rejected.
TR-2 Result tenant/org/actor scope must equal authoritative request scope; the structurally valid cross-org result fixture must be rejected.
TR-3 Result marking must be no higher than request clearance on both classification and TLP axes; the structurally valid clearance-exceeded fixture must be rejected.
TR-4 Available result full alert_ref type/id/version/digest and context alert_id/alert_digest must equal the request; the structurally valid mismatch fixture must be rejected.
TR-5 Authorization binding must match tenant, full org scope, full actor identity, capability/schema/input/policy digests; the result must echo request idempotency key and exact binding.
TR-6 context_digest must equal SHA-256(JCS(available_result_projection)) produced by SOC after authorization/redaction.
runtime_only_declared: TR-7 Runtime must produce the identical unavailable response class, timing budget and observable audit behavior for absent, unauthorized and policy-filtered resources to avoid side-channel existence leakage. Static schema fixtures prove only the response shape, not timing or operational behavior.
TR-8 Runtime must resolve org hierarchy and membership from SOC-owned authoritative state and must never trust include_descendants from the request body as an authorization decision.
TR-9 Runtime audit must record policy/capability/input/output digests without exposing sensitive context to unauthorized callers.

member_set_integrity.algorithm: MEMBER-SET-SHA256/v1: reduce every entry of members[] to exactly {file, kind, contract_version, sha256}, sort the reduced entries by file in Unicode code point order, serialize that array as RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON, and render member_set_digest as sha256:<lowercase hex SHA-256 over those UTF-8 bytes>. The digest input is derived from members[] only: member_set_integrity itself and every other manifest key are excluded, so the aggregate is non-circular and is recomputed without reading its own declared value.

verification.scope: Standalone static evidence only. The suite in tools/contract-validation/tests/validate-alert-context.test.mjs holds 19 adversarial rejection cases plus 2 positive checks; several adversarial cases are table-driven over multiple mutations and every mutation must fail closed. It proves packet, schema, fixture, authorization-binding, lifecycle-coherence, member-hash and member-set integrity only: no endpoint, Fabric grant, W2-F delegation, runtime enforcement or release certification is demonstrated, and lifecycle acceptance is a recorded decision rather than evidence.
verification.dependency_root_override_env: CYBRIK_CONTRACT_VALIDATION_DEPS_ROOT=<directory whose node_modules already provides ajv 8.20.0 and ajv-formats 3.0.1>. All three commands run from the repository root, install nothing and require no network.
verification.coverage_floor: Branch coverage of tools/contract-validation/validate-alert-context.mjs must stay at or above 80% under the declared standalone coverage command.
verification.ci_wiring: NOT WIRED. Canonical CI wiring (npm script registration in tools/contract-validation/package.json plus pipeline invocation) is deliberately out of scope for this acceptance and belongs to a later integration gate. This packet adds no tracked file and modifies none.

acceptance.scope_of_acceptance: Accepts the business payload shape, the RFC 8785/JCS projections and the static packet integrity evidence as the basis for implementation. It does not open the transport/endpoint, capability-registry, Fabric invocation-grant, consumer-integration, CI-wiring or release-certification gates; each of those remains a separate gate requiring its own explicit approval. Acceptance changes no runtime behavior and proves none.
settled_checklist: A1 SOC owns alert truth and the exact alert-context field projection.
A2 Tenant/org/actor/clearance derive from authenticated SOC policy; body values are advisory copies only.
A3 The available result marking must never exceed request clearance on either axis.

A4 Unavailable behavior must be indistinguishable for absent, unauthorized and filtered resources, including timing and audit side channels; this stays an unproven runtime obligation, tracked as TR-7.
A5 Fabric tool-grant authority remains in the accepted Fabric execution chain and W2-F inference delegation cannot authorize this capability.
A6 Capability pin name/version/digest, R0 classification and side_effects=false are exact and fixed.
A7 All static schema, fixture, authorization-binding, semantic-witness, member-hash and member-set checks pass from a clean checkout under the declared standalone commands.
A8 Authorization-before-cache, tenant-partitioned replay, exact binding match and fail-closed conflict rejection are the required runtime semantics.
A9 SOC owns the RFC 8785/JCS projections and context_digest production after authorization and redaction.
A10 The separate transport/endpoint/registry and consumer implementation gates are NOT opened by this acceptance and each remains deferred to its own gate.

residual_questions: Should the first implementation return only digest-bound related-object references, as proposed, or a separately bounded field-level snapshot profile?
Which SOC permission is authoritative for include_descendants and should R0 v0.1.0 prohibit descendant aggregation until that permission contract is accepted?
What constant-time or bounded-jitter target is required for unavailable responses to make no-existence-leak operationally testable?
Which signing/attestation key and receipt field, if any, should bind the SOC-produced context_digest beyond its SHA-256 integrity anchor?
Does the first transport bind this business payload to the existing Fabric tool-execution envelope, or does a separate read-capability binding need proposal and acceptance?
